title: 10. Conclusion to Part II: The Future of a Mutually Flourishing Economy through Hwajaeng
content:
This study has presented, as a survival strategy for humanity in the AI era, a new paradigm that combines correlative thinking and *hwajaeng*. In Part I, through the four modes of correlative thinking—multidimensionality (立體), circulation (循環), empathy (共感), and convergence (融合)—we confirmed the distinctive strengths of the human in the AI era. In Part II, we showed how these four modes of correlative thinking correspond exactly to the four-gate structure of Wonhyo's *hwajaeng* theory—the Gate of Arising-and-Ceasing (spring), the Gate of the Three Natures (summer), the Gate of Suchness (autumn), and the Pure Land Gate (winter)—and applied this to the *hwajaeng* integration of four economic theories.

*Hwajaeng* conveys the following message to humanity in the AI era. Different perspectives each hold their own validity, and *hwajaeng* is not a way in which one annihilates the others, but a mutual subsumption and integration at a higher dimension.

The mutually flourishing, connected economy (相生連結經濟) embodies the principle of *hwajaeng* in the economic domain. When libertarian freedom, utilitarian efficiency, social-contractarian justice, and communitarian solidarity are integrated circularly like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, the economy of the AI era can be converted into a mutually flourishing economy in which all of humanity survives together.

Just as the liberation and cessation of Buddhism possess a dynamic stillness in which body and mind are completely unified, the logic of *hwajaeng* is humanity's distinctive wisdom that leads the conflicts and oppositions of the AI era to an integration at a higher dimension.
